title: Accounts docs
intro: Accounts is the sign-up and sign-in system of your own website and admin: one user list for your shoppers and your staff, with roles. Visitors sign in with the widget or with your own screens on the API; your server and our other products check their sign-ins offline with your website's public keys. Your website's tokens are in the Portal: open the website, then Install and tokens. The browser token is public and goes into your pages; the server token is secret and stays on your server.
localhost: Testing on your own computer: the browser token also works on pages served from localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], on any port, over http or https. These pages use your website's real database, keys and providers, so the accounts made there are real. There is no test mode.
methods: Sign-in methods are features: Phone code (a code by SMS or WhatsApp), Phone + password, Email + password, Email code / magic link, Google, Apple and Facebook. Turn on the ones you want; the widget shows exactly those. Phone code and Phone + password share the phone format (default calling code and trunk prefix, Settings → Phone numbers). Codes, magic links, password resets and invites are sent through Notifications: paste your website's Notifications server token into Connections and write these templates in Notifications (keys below, with the values each one gets). Phone + password's Forgot password sends accounts.phone_code on the Phone code channel; with Forgot password off, its link opens your own page (for example a WhatsApp chat). Without Notifications, those steps answer notifications_not_connected. Phone codes wait between sends (cooldownSeconds, refusal code_cooldown with retryAt), are capped per number and per website each hour (code_limit), may be limited to your countries (country_not_allowed), and a new user without a name gets the newUserName template ({last4}: the number's last 4 digits).
social: Google, Apple and Facebook use your own app keys (Connections). Register the return address below with the provider. The widget opens the provider's page; the provider sends the person back to Accounts, which finds or creates the user and returns the browser to your page with a single-use code in the address fragment; the widget exchanges it for the sign-in.
signIns: A sign-in is a JWT signed with EdDSA (Ed25519) that lasts 15 minutes: iss is Accounts' address, aud is your website id, sub is the user id, and it carries name, email, phone and, with Roles and permissions on, role and permissions (* = every permission). The widget renews it with the user's session (session length and remember me are set per role; defaults 1 day and 30 days). Verify it on your server with the public keys (no call per check), and paste the Accounts server token into other products so they trust sign-ins too. A sign-in only says who the user is: it never authorises admin actions in any product — those need your server token or a ticket.
visitorApi: Headless: build your own screens on the visitor API with the browser token. Routes of a signed-in user also take the sign-in in the SS-Sign-In header. Sign-in routes answer { status: signed_in, signIn, expiresAt, refreshToken, sessionExpiresAt, user }, { status: two_step, challenge }, { status: two_step_setup, challenge, secret, otpauthUrl } or { status: pending }. Keep the refresh token in the browser and renew with POST /v1/session/refresh.
roles: One user list: every new sign-up gets the Customer role; GET /v1/users/count and /v1/users/counts?by=status|role count it with the list's filters (q, role, roles, permission, status, blocked, deletion, phone, phoneDigits, createdAfter). The ready-made roles (Owner, Business manager, Product manager, Marketing manager, Support staff) start with default permissions from Accounts, Chat, Notifications and Ecommerce (Owner has every permission), can be changed and copied, and you can add your own. A role's permissions come from the products whose server tokens you pasted into Accounts (each product publishes its list), plus your own permission names (site:<name>). A role also sets two-step (optional or required), the session length and remember me, and: rank (a smaller number ranks higher: Owner 100, Business manager 200, Product manager 300, Marketing manager 400, Support staff 500, Customer 900; your own roles sit between 101 and 899), remember (ask, ask_ticked, or always: no box, always remembered), methods (the sign-in methods its users may use; [] = all; others get method_refused), signIn (on, or paused: its users, and new sign-ups while Customer is paused, get sign_in_paused with your paused text, before any code is sent) and logSignIns (sign-ins, failures with their IP, resets and recovery-code use go to the activity log). Your admin checks the user's role and permissions before it asks a product for a ticket.
rules: Sign-up rules (Approval / invite sign-up): open sign-up, invite only, or approval required, and which standard fields are required. Custom fields (text, number, date, choice) are set in the dashboard. Profile settings (shown while any sign-in method is on): addresses per user (up to 10), keep at least one address, and the required address fields; addresses have an area and one default address. Security: password rules (length up to 128, the breached-password check, Phone + password's letter-and-digit rule, and the personal check that refuses the name, the e-mail's local part or runs like 1234 or qwer), a fixed or growing lock after repeated wrong passwords (growing: 1 minute, doubling up to 60), a limit of tries per network and address per 15 minutes, two-step sign-in with recovery codes, risk checks against disposable e-mail addresses and many accounts from one device or network, and terms acceptance (the version each user accepted is kept).
dataRights: Download my data gives the user one single-use link (15 minutes) to everything Accounts and every product whose token you pasted keep about them. Delete my account waits for your approval in the Users admin widget (or for the days set in Settings), then erases the user here and in every connected product; a product that cannot be reached is asked again on later requests.
activity: Activity log copy: paste this website's Accounts server token into your other products; each one then sends every staff action to Accounts: who (with the acting user's role), what, the target and its label (for example an order number), a short detail and when — never message contents, secrets or addresses. Read the copies with GET /v1/activity-copies?productId=&actor=&action=&target=&q=&from=&to= (newest first; action takes one action or several separated by commas, q searches labels, details, names and targets, from and to take an ISO-8601 time or a day in your business.json time zone) and count them with GET /v1/activity-copies/count and /v1/activity-copies/counts?by=productId|action|actor. Accounts' own log (users and roles, with each user's name or role as the label) is read with GET /v1/activity.
orders: Orders tab: paste the Ecommerce server token; My account then lists the user's last 20 orders from Ecommerce (GET /v1/customers/<userId>/orders on Ecommerce, with the server token you pasted): number, status (the status label your shop set) and total.
staff: Staff and customers from your server: POST /v1/users creates an active user { name, email?, phone?, role?, password?, addresses?, notes?, custom? } and sends nothing (an e-mail address or a phone number is needed); PATCH /v1/users/:id also changes email and phone (normalised, unique, marked verified; null removes one), password (the user is signed out everywhere) and addresses; DELETE /v1/users/:id { reason } erases the user at once here and in every connected product. Answers carry hasPassword, roleSince, lockedUntil and recoveryCodesLeft. GET /v1/users?permission=<product>:<key>&blocked=false lists the unblocked users whose role grants a permission (products' staff alerts read it). Guards, always, when the call names the acting user (SS-Actor-Id, the Accounts user id) or comes with a ticket: nobody changes their own role, blocks or deletes themselves; nobody edits, blocks or deletes a user whose role ranks above theirs, or gives a role ranking above theirs; the last unblocked Owner is never demoted, blocked or deleted (403 forbidden). Without an acting user your server token stays all-powerful.
serverSignIn: Sign-in from your server: every sign-in, sign-up, code, renew and sign-out route also takes your server token with the visitor's address in SS-Visitor-IP (required on writes; it drives the per-visitor limits and the risk checks) and, optionally, the visitor's browser in SS-Visitor-Agent (the device list names it). The answer carries the refresh token in the body for your server to keep; renew with POST /v1/session/refresh. Routes of a signed-in user take the sign-in in SS-Sign-In as usual.
legacy: Passwords from another system (importers): bcrypt hashes ($2a$, $2b$, $2y$, any cost) and PBKDF2 hashes written as pbkdf2$<iterations>$<salt>$<hash> (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 of <pepper>:<password>, base64) sign in as they are; paste that system's pepper into Connections → Pepper of imported passwords. After the first good sign-in the password is saved the Accounts way. Imported two-step sign-in keeps its authenticator secret, and its old recovery codes (sha256 of recovery: and the code) each work once.
install: Add the script to the pages of your website and place the visitor widgets where they should appear: sign_in, my_account, and role_request (Role requests: visitors ask for a role, for example membership). The sign-in widget also takes setup links (?ss_setup=<code> on its page). Widgets render nothing while their features are off or the product is stopped.
admin: Admin widgets run in your own admin with a ticket. Users (users.read to see, users.manage to change): status chips with their counts, search and filters, each user's detail, Add user, Edit (contacts, password, notes, custom fields, addresses), Invite (sent, or the link handed to you), and in its More menu a sign-in code and a setup link (Staff sign-in codes and setup links), sign out everywhere, approve or decline a sign-up, keep or delete on a deletion request, block, and Delete user behind a typed confirmation; with Role requests on, the requests list with invite, decline and open again. Roles (roles.manage). Activity (activity.read, Activity log copy): every product's copies with counts per product and filters. Include the script without data-token, place the widgets and register your ticket function. The widget calls it at start and 1 minute before the ticket expires; your server checks the user's sign-in and role every time.
tickets: Your server asks for a ticket with the server token (never send the server token to a browser). The origin is the address of your admin page: any https origin, or a local one while testing. Tickets last 15 minutes and carry only the permissions of switched-on features.
business: Every product reads your business basics from https://<your domain>/.well-known/business.json. Only name is required; without the file the name is your domain and the time zone is UTC.
api: Every route answers JSON; errors are RFC 9457 problems with a stable code. Lists are paged with cursor and limit. Routes of a feature that is off answer 403 feature_off.

phone_password: Routes: POST /v1/sign-up/phone-password, POST /v1/sign-in/phone-password { phone, password, remember }, POST /v1/password/phone/forgot { phone } and POST /v1/password/phone/reset { phone, code, password }. PUT /v1/me/password also serves users with a phone number. Settings: visitors can sign up (off: only you give passwords, through Add user, setup links and invites; sign-up answers sign_up_closed), minimum length (6–128), letter and digit, breached-password check, wrong passwords before a lock, the lock, Forgot password (code or off) and the Forgot password page.
staff_links: POST /v1/users/:id/sign-in-code answers { code, expiresAt }: 6 digits for staff to read to the user, never sent, single use, typed into the phone-code, e-mail-code or phone + password screen; a new one cancels the old. POST /v1/users/:id/setup-link answers { url, expiresAt }: it lets the user choose a password (also without an e-mail address) through POST /v1/setup-links/accept { code, password }, which signs them in; using the link proves the user's phone number (you send the link to it, so their guest orders and points join the account) and signs their other devices out. Set your setup page with {code} (for example https://shop.com/account/setup/{code}); without one the link opens your website with ?ss_setup=, which the sign-in widget takes. POST /v1/users/invite takes deliver: return to answer the invite link instead of sending it. Each is logged with the acting user.
role_requests: Visitors ask with POST /v1/role-requests { role, name, phone | email, note } (no account; the roles you list in Settings). Your server and the Users widget read GET /v1/role-requests?status=pending|invited|completed|declined|expired (with counts), and POST /v1/role-requests/:id/invite (creates the user, or gives the role to the user with that phone or e-mail, and answers a setup link unless they already have a password; a user who never proved that phone or e-mail gets nothing and the invite answers 409 contact_unverified until you check with the person, confirm it on their user or remove that account), /decline and /reopen. A request is completed when the password is set or the role given; expired when its setup link ran out. Users carry roleSince (Member since).
